news.title: AI Can Now Design Viruses. We Need Biosecurity Guardrails Now
news.summary_en: As AI advances, the risk of engineered viral bioweapons is growing. The window to prepare is now—by building a layered, resilient system of defense.

news.title: Buying Time Against AI Proliferation: The Economics of Governed Access
news.summary_en: The author describes a formal model of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and proliferation that focuses on the demand for AI capability.

news.title: When Disaster Strikes, Could AI Help? Q&A with Jessica Jensen
news.summary_en: Disasters are more frequent, more severe, and more costly. Pressure is mounting on emergency managers and the organizations that support them. Senior policy researcher Jessica Jensen discusses how artificial intelligence could help carry some of that burden.

news.title: Countering Model Distillation: Limits and Alternatives
news.summary_en: Artificial intelligence model distillation (training new models on outputs of more capable ones) could affect U.S. frontier model advantage. New policy tools could augment such technical countermeasures as raising costs or reducing model quality.

news.title: A Standardized Framework for Assessing High-Risk Life Sciences Research: Defining Objective Criteria That Can Facilitate Expert and AI Reviews of Dangerous Gain-of-Function Research
news.summary_en: Recent federal policies establish funding prohibitions and review requirements for certain high-risk life sciences research. The authors advise that federal agencies adopt an objective decisionmaking framework for dangerous gain-of-function research.

news.title: Operational reliance on AI in supply chains and emerging insurance risks
news.summary_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming embedded in supply chains. This report examines how that changes operational reliance, resilience, and insurance risk across logistics, transport, and warehousing.
